lean_implies_source.reasoning: Encode each source Bernoulli X_i by a Boolean B_i with true corresponding to 1 and false to 0, and index the N variables by a finite type. The Lean sum is S_N, each integral is E exp(lambda X_i), and the hypotheses include source mutual independence and lambda > 0, so the Lean inequality specializes exactly to (2.7) in the source's t > E S_N context.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: Every measurable Boolean B_i is a Bernoulli random variable with parameter P(B_i = true), so equation (2.7) applies after reindexing whenever t exceeds E S. If t <= E S, Jensen gives product_i E exp(lambda X_i) >= exp(lambda E S), hence the Lean right side is at least exp(lambda(E S - t)) >= 1 and the probability bound follows from P <= 1. The empty family follows directly by splitting t <= 0 and t > 0. Thus the source result plus its standard probability semantics covers all Lean cases; the extra cases add no nonvacuous strength.

rationale: The target states exactly the exponential-Markov product bound in display (2.7): the Boolean indicator sum is S_N, iIndepFun is mutual independence, each integral is E exp(lambda X_i), and the prefactor is exp(-lambda t). The source's Bernoulli coordinates are exactly measurable Boolean variables after 0/1 recoding. Although the target omits the enclosing theorem's t > E S_N condition and allows empty indexing, those additional cases satisfy the same inequality automatically and carry no nontrivial extra content. Both implication directions therefore hold and the appropriate classification is faithful-equivalent.
